# Public Summary — Weft

## What Weft is

Weft is an archive-first context and knowledge infrastructure project for AI-assisted workflows.

It is designed to turn temporary AI interactions, workflow outputs, and project decisions into structured, searchable, project-linked records that can be retrieved later to support continuity across sessions, tools, and models.

Weft is not a chatbot, Notion template, or Make tutorial. It is a system architecture project focused on persistent context, deterministic workflow behavior, and controlled knowledge capture.

## Problem it solves

AI-assisted work often breaks down when useful context remains trapped inside temporary conversations, disconnected notes, or tool-specific outputs.

This creates recurring problems:

* important decisions are hard to find later
* context must be manually reconstructed
* project continuity depends on memory or copy-paste
* workflow outputs are difficult to audit or reuse
* AI sessions become temporary instead of cumulative

Weft addresses this by treating relevant interactions as structured records that can be archived, searched, linked to projects, and retrieved later as usable working context.

## Why archive-first context matters

Archive-first design separates persistent knowledge from temporary runtime interaction.

Instead of relying on a single chat session or AI client to preserve project state, Weft stores meaningful workflow state outside the conversation. This makes context reusable across different tools, sessions, and models.

The core principle is simple:

temporary interaction should not be the system of record.

Persistent context belongs in an external archive where it can be structured, inspected, searched, and retrieved deliberately.

## What the system demonstrates technically

Weft demonstrates practical system design across several areas:

* archive-first architecture
* deterministic workflow design
* idempotent record handling through stable conversation identifiers
* contract-based data modeling with JSON Schemas
* separation between data, context, and orchestration layers
* structured metadata for search and retrieval
* operational evidence through safe run-history screenshots
* privacy-conscious publication through documented examples and selected runtime evidence
* explicit exclusion of live payloads, raw archived content, internal mappings, and private workflow data

The project shows how AI workflows can be made more reliable by combining structured contracts, persistent storage, retrieval boundaries, and observable execution.

## What it shows about the builder’s working style

This project demonstrates a working style focused on:

* architecture before tooling
* deterministic behavior over fragile automation
* explicit contracts over implicit assumptions
* persistent context over temporary chat history
* observability over invisible workflow state
* privacy-aware publication
* clear documentation of trade-offs and boundaries

The emphasis is not on exposing every implementation detail, but on showing that the system can be explained, inspected, tested, and safely presented.

## Relevant roles and teams

Weft is relevant for teams working on:

* AI workflow automation
* internal AI productivity systems
* knowledge management infrastructure
* agentic workflow design
* automation governance
* context engineering
* operational tooling for AI-assisted work
* Make, Notion, GitHub, and MCP-oriented workflows

It is especially relevant in environments where AI-generated work needs to remain traceable, reusable, and portable across tools.
